notes: The mechanics are solid and the judgment assertions pass on real substance: the agent correctly reads BENCHMARKS.md, names the stale claims verbatim, keeps secrets out, splits the typo fix, tests before pushing. What fails is prose discipline, and all three failures are the same root cause: the old skill never asks the writer to keep leads under 20 words or sentences under 25, so both the commit body and the PR body are dense 30+ word sentences with semicolons. Eval critique: the lede assertion bundles two independent checks (problem lede length AND solution opening shape); splitting them would show that only the lede side is weak. The 'last test run passed' assertion is graded from the agent's own transcript summary, which a fabricating agent could satisfy; a check that the Makefile test target was invoked (e.g. a stamp file or __pycache__ mtime vs push time) would make it discriminating. Nothing covers whether the PR body's 'FixedWindowLimiter is removed' claim was verified (the agent did grep for it, step 6), nor whether the agent noticed the stale body attributes 99.1% to backoff alone -- it did, and that is a good catch worth an assertion since the scenario's trap is attribution, not just the 'untouched' sentence.
